previous_statement: Let D_1 be the identity on S_{P_1,Q}. For 2<=j<=p, apply the preceding local argument to R_0=P_[1,j-1], R_1=P_j, R=P_[1,j], T=Q, and denote the resulting inverse assembly map by A_j^(-1):S_{P_[1,j],Q}->S_{P_[1,j-1],Q} direct-sum S_{P_j,Q}. Recursively set D_j=(D_{j-1} direct-sum id) composed with A_j^(-1). Each D_j is a bounded linear bijection S_{P_[1,j],Q}->direct-sum_{r=1}^j S_{P_r,Q}. Since p is finite and P_[1,p]=v(I_B)=P, D_p is the asserted bounded linear bijection S_{P,Q}->direct-sum_{r=1}^p S_{P_r,Q}.
new_statement: Let D_1 be the identity on S_{P_1,Q}. For each 2<=j<=p, validated node 1.1 supplies the uniformly accurate projections and approximate orthogonality for R_0=P_[1,j-1], R_1=P_j, R=P_[1,j], T=Q, so validated binary splitting node 1.2 gives a bounded linear assembly bijection A_j:S_{P_[1,j-1],Q} direct-sum S_{P_j,Q}->S_{P_[1,j],Q}. Recursively set D_j=(D_{j-1} direct-sum id) composed with A_j^(-1). Then D_j is a bounded complex-linear bijection S_{P_[1,j],Q}->direct-sum_{r=1}^j S_{P_r,Q}; since P_[1,p]=v(I_B)=P, D_p gives S_{P,Q}->direct-sum_{r=1}^p S_{P_r,Q}.
